Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The Season 14 Storm Shred Druid read forward onto the 3.2.0 PTR, and this page has to open with the bad news because it is the whole story. 3.2.0 guts Storm Shepherd's Call from roughly a 1.2 million percent multiplier to 80%, and cuts Might of the Ursine from 13% to 4%. Storm Shepherd's Call is the entire reason Season 14's Shred Druid existed: it is what made Spirit regeneration scale damage and inverted the build's whole gearing logic. Removing it does not adjust this build, it retires the archetype - the digest says so in those words - and the +30% Druid core stat scalar (1.25 to 1.625) does not begin to compensate, because a baseline additive buff cannot replace a gutted multiplier. Both 3.2.0 class tier reads agree Druid is among the losers of the patch, though they disagree by a tier on how far it falls (aoeah B, mtmmo C). So why is this page here? Because the owner's requirement is that every class carries a build, and the honest options were this or nothing: no 3.2.0 build guide exists on any major English site, no 3.2.0 skill allocation or paragon ordering is published for any class, and inventing a replacement Druid build would be fabrication rather than research. This is therefore the Season 14 build with its Season 14 numbers, carried forward with its own obituary attached. Use it to understand what the Druid was and what the patch takes away; do not read it as a recommendation for 3.2.0. When Season 15 ships, expect this file to be rebuilt around a different skill entirely rather than re-tuned. Two Season 14 caveats also carry forward: survivability is the Druid's named weakness, and Maxroll attributed part of Storm Shepherd's Season 14 dominance to bugs - including that clicking Shred beat holding it - which is context for why the multiplier was cut this hard.

Rotation
  1. Toggle Lightning Storm and Hurricane on, enter Grizzly Rage whenever it is available, refresh Debilitating Roar before it expires, then click Shred as fast as you can - never hold the button.
  2. Watch Cyclone Armor uptime and Grizzly Rage windows as the tiers climb.
Variants

Leveling — Cyclone Armor up, Debilitating Roar before contact, Grizzly Rage on elites, Shred everything, Wind Shear whenever Spirit runs dry.
Move on when [ptr] Reach the point where you can equip a Berú of the Red Wolf Moon, the documented stand-in until Berú of the Storm Shepherd drops. On the PTR, Mrak simply hands you the gear.

Early Endgame — Toggle Lightning Storm and Hurricane on, enter Grizzly Rage whenever available, refresh Debilitating Roar before it expires, then click Shred as fast as you can - do not hold the button, because rapid casts let Waxing Gibbous's extra attacks re-trigger the set bonus. [ptr] Note that this click-don't-hold interaction is one of the behaviours Maxroll described as a bug in Season 14, and 3.2.0's cut to Storm Shepherd's Call is the patch responding to that whole package.
Move on when [ptr] Berú of the Storm Shepherd equipped. In Season 14 this was the moment the build began - after it, the Spirit-regeneration-scales-damage rule took over and the entire affix priority changed. On the 3.2.0 PTR that rule is what has been cut from roughly 1.2 million percent to 80%, so expect the transition to be barely noticeable rather than transformative.

Late Endgame — Unchanged from the early endgame: Lightning Storm and Hurricane on, Grizzly Rage on cooldown, Debilitating Roar refreshed, Shred clicked rather than held. PocQue runes for the Earthen Bulwark barrier and Unstoppable, which also feeds Tibault's Will.
Move on when [ptr] In Season 14 this was a gear-tuning gate rather than a rotation change - full Mythic priority list and masterworking. It carries forward unchanged because 3.2.0 publishes nothing that would move it.

Pushing — As the late endgame, played with more care about Grizzly Rage windows and Cyclone Armor uptime. Click Shred, never hold it.

Lootfilter

Druid Companion Endgame — D4 Loot Filter — View Filter

diablo4lootfilter.com

[ptr] Carried from the Season 14 build, and it was already an approximate match there: the site exposes no Shred or Storm-Shepherd-tagged permalink, so this is a same-class endgame code for a different Druid build. Preview its rules before importing and confirm it is not filtering out Berú of the Storm Shepherd set pieces or Spirit-regen affixes. On the PTR the point is largely moot - Mrak hands testers gear directly - and if 3.2.0's Storm Shepherd's Call cut ships as written, a Shred-tuned filter will not be what you want anyway.

Uniques
  • pants [ptr] On the PTR, take it from the vendor Mrak beside the main Waypoint: his PTR Boosts hand out uniques, maxed aspects, all runes, glyphs, level 70 and the seasonal items outright, so farming is not the test here. Expected live route, carried forward from Season 14: No dedicated boss - it sits in the General Unique Pool, so farm it via the Horadric Cube: Common pants plus Primordial Dust rerolls into a random pants-slot unique. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Re-verify at launch. Where →

How to run them

[ptr] Carried over from Season 14 unchanged, which is sourced rather than assumed: mercenaries are not mentioned anywhere in the official 3.2.0 notes, so the Season 14 pairings are the only guidance that exists. The Season 14 reasoning: every one of the guide's profiles hires Raheir and takes Ground Slam, Bastion, Iron Wolf's Virtue and Raheir's Aegis - what you are buying is Valiance, a rotating cheat-death, and this build needs it because survivability is the acknowledged Druid weakness. Varyana reinforces on Bloodthirst for attack speed, which on a build whose damage came from clicking Shred as fast as possible was a direct damage gain. Icy Veins takes the other branch and reinforces with Aldkin on Field of Languish for damage reduction instead; take Aldkin if you are dying.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The Season 14 Storm Shred Druid read forward onto the 3.2.0 PTR, and this page has to open with the bad news because it is the whole story. 3.2.0 guts Storm Shepherd's Call from roughly a 1.2 million percent multiplier to 80%, and cuts Might of the Ursine from 13% to 4%. Storm Shepherd's Call is the entire reason Season 14's Shred Druid existed: it is what made Spirit regeneration scale damage and inverted the build's whole gearing logic. Removing it does not adjust this build, it retires the archetype - the digest says so in those words - and the +30% Druid core stat scalar (1.25 to 1.625) does not begin to compensate, because a baseline additive buff cannot replace a gutted multiplier. Both 3.2.0 class tier reads agree Druid is among the losers of the patch, though they disagree by a tier on how far it falls (aoeah B, mtmmo C). So why is this page here? Because the owner's requirement is that every class carries a build, and the honest options were this or nothing: no 3.2.0 build guide exists on any major English site, no 3.2.0 skill allocation or paragon ordering is published for any class, and inventing a replacement Druid build would be fabrication rather than research. This is therefore the Season 14 build with its Season 14 numbers, carried forward with its own obituary attached. Use it to understand what the Druid was and what the patch takes away; do not read it as a recommendation for 3.2.0. When Season 15 ships, expect this file to be rebuilt around a different skill entirely rather than re-tuned. Two Season 14 caveats also carry forward: survivability is the Druid's named weakness, and Maxroll attributed part of Storm Shepherd's Season 14 dominance to bugs - including that clicking Shred beat holding it - which is context for why the multiplier was cut this hard.

Rotation
  1. Toggle Lightning Storm and Hurricane on, enter Grizzly Rage whenever it is available, refresh Debilitating Roar before it expires, then click Shred as fast as you can - never hold the button.
  2. Watch Cyclone Armor uptime and Grizzly Rage windows as the tiers climb.
Variants

Leveling — Cyclone Armor up, Debilitating Roar before contact, Grizzly Rage on elites, Shred everything, Wind Shear whenever Spirit runs dry.
Move on when [ptr] Reach the point where you can equip a Berú of the Red Wolf Moon, the documented stand-in until Berú of the Storm Shepherd drops. On the PTR, Mrak simply hands you the gear.

Early Endgame — Toggle Lightning Storm and Hurricane on, enter Grizzly Rage whenever available, refresh Debilitating Roar before it expires, then click Shred as fast as you can - do not hold the button, because rapid casts let Waxing Gibbous's extra attacks re-trigger the set bonus. [ptr] Note that this click-don't-hold interaction is one of the behaviours Maxroll described as a bug in Season 14, and 3.2.0's cut to Storm Shepherd's Call is the patch responding to that whole package.
Move on when [ptr] Berú of the Storm Shepherd equipped. In Season 14 this was the moment the build began - after it, the Spirit-regeneration-scales-damage rule took over and the entire affix priority changed. On the 3.2.0 PTR that rule is what has been cut from roughly 1.2 million percent to 80%, so expect the transition to be barely noticeable rather than transformative.

Late Endgame — Unchanged from the early endgame: Lightning Storm and Hurricane on, Grizzly Rage on cooldown, Debilitating Roar refreshed, Shred clicked rather than held. PocQue runes for the Earthen Bulwark barrier and Unstoppable, which also feeds Tibault's Will.
Move on when [ptr] In Season 14 this was a gear-tuning gate rather than a rotation change - full Mythic priority list and masterworking. It carries forward unchanged because 3.2.0 publishes nothing that would move it.

Pushing — As the late endgame, played with more care about Grizzly Rage windows and Cyclone Armor uptime. Click Shred, never hold it.

Uniques
  • pants [ptr] On the PTR, take it from the vendor Mrak beside the main Waypoint: his PTR Boosts hand out uniques, maxed aspects, all runes, glyphs, level 70 and the seasonal items outright, so farming is not the test here. Expected live route, carried forward from Season 14: No dedicated boss - it sits in the General Unique Pool, so farm it via the Horadric Cube: Common pants plus Primordial Dust rerolls into a random pants-slot unique. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Expected live route, carried forward from Season 14: Target-farm Harbinger of Hatred at Greater Lair tier for the base item, then craft the Mythic version - it is what lets Shred be cast inside Grizzly Rage. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Re-verify at launch. Where →

Provoke

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 25 seconds

Raheir Taunts enemies around you for 5 seconds. You gain 5% Damage Reduction for each target, up to 20%.

Ground Slam

Core skillRaheir

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Round Shield

Basic Attack: Shield Strike

Raheir brutalizes the ground, dealing 160% Physical damage and Slowing enemies by 30% for 6 seconds. Targets in the center of the slam are Slowed by 60% instead.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Raheir swings a round shield at enemies, dealing 85% Physical damage. Every 20 swings, Raheir Heals you for 8% of your Maximum Life.

Shield Charge

Core skillRaheir

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Tower Shield

Basic Attack: Shield Bash

Raheir rushes forward aggressively, dealing 110% Physical damage and Taunting nearby enemies for 4 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Raheir bashes enemies with a tower shield, dealing 80% Physical damage and Fortifying you for 0.2% of your Maximum Life.

Crater

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Raheir strikes the ground 3 times, each burst dealing 30% Physical damage and Pulling In enemies. The final burst deals 40% more Physical damage and additionally Stuns enemies for 2 seconds.

Raheir's Guard

PassiveRaheir

Raheir grants you 15%[+] Armor.

Vanguard

PassiveRaheir

Raheir Slows surrounding enemies by 40%.

Mocking Lure

PassiveRaheir

You deal 15%[x] increased damage to enemies Taunted by Raheir.

Iron Wolf's Ward

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he Knocks Back Close enemies and Taunts Distant enemies for 4 seconds.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Iron Wolf's Call

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, your next 4 Core Skills within 10 seconds deal 25%[x] increased damage and cost no Resource.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 25%.

Sundering Shield

PassiveRaheir

Raheir's final Crater burst deals 200%[x] increased damage and inflicts Vulnerable on enemies for 4 seconds.

Shield Throw

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Consecrated Shield

PassiveRaheir

Raheir's Shield Throw Consecrates enemies for 6 seconds. Directly damaging a Consecrated enemy Heals you for 6% of your Maximum Life, once per target.

Bastion

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 30 seconds

Raheir takes a protective position for 5 seconds, redirecting 90% of the damage that would be dealt to surrounding allies to himself for 5 seconds.

Bastion's initial cast also grants surrounding allies Unstoppable for 1.0 seconds.
